column5: source
column6: target

column5: Oh, really...?\nI guess I'll try being strong for you.\nYou have a ton of other burdens to worry about.
column6: 哦，真的吗……？\n那我就试着为你坚强起来吧。\n你还有一大堆别的重担要操心呢。

column5: Oh, so I'm not alone?\nThat's more of a relief than you know, [firstname].\nWhen and {i}if{/i} the time comes? We'll handle it together.
column6: 哦，原来我并不孤单？\n这让我松了一大口气，比你知道的还要多，[firstname]。\n等到——{i}如果{/i}真到了那一天？我们一起面对。

column5: Oh, so I'm not alone?\nThat's more of a relief than you know, [firstname].\nWhen and {i}if{/i} the time comes? We'll handle it together.
column6: 哦，原来我并不孤单？\n这让我松了一大口气，比你知道的还要多，[firstname]。\n等到——{i}如果{/i}真到了那一天？我们一起面对。

column5: Hey Zamira, about those antlers.
column6: 嘿，扎米拉，关于你头上那对鹿角。

column5: What about them?
column6: 它们怎么了？

column5: You ever like, hit them on a doorway?\nI mean, you can't be fully aware of them all the time.\nOh! Have you ever accidentally hit someone else with them?
column6: 你有没有，呃，撞到过门框上？\n我是说，你也不可能时时刻刻都留意到它们。\n哦！你有没有不小心用它们撞到过别人？

column5: I'm about to...
column6: 我马上就要……

column5: Whoa, okay, backing off...!\nI was just curious. I've always wondered.\nHow do you put a shirt on each morning?
column6: 哇，好，我退后……！\n我只是好奇。我一直都想知道。\n你每天早上是怎么穿衣服的？

column5: What do you mean?
column6: 什么意思？

column5: Well you can't really slip clothes over your head.\nThose things would tear through any fabric.
column6: 你想啊，你没法把衣服从头上套进去。\n那些东西会把任何布料都戳穿的。

column5: I don't really have anything that slips over my head.\nI only wear things I can put my arms inside of first.\nYou know, like button ups, or vests?
column6: 我基本上没有能从头上套的东西。\n我只穿那种能先把胳膊伸进去的。\n就是说，像系扣的衬衫，或者马甲？

column5: Right. I guess that makes sense.\nSorry for annoying you. Please don't hit me!
column6: 对。我猜这说得通。\n抱歉烦到你了。求你别撞我！

column5: Of course. I'll do my best, Fortaime.\nBut I'm not responsible for any \"accidents\".
column6: 当然。我会尽量的，福泰姆。\n但任何“意外”我可概不负责。

column5: Hey, Zamira. What's work like?
column6: 嘿，扎米拉。你的工作是什么样的？

column5: It's a lot less exciting than you'd think.\nThey advertise it as a position of power.\nBusting smugglers, and protecting Valinorth.
column6: 比你以为的要无聊得多。\n他们把它宣传成一种有权力的职位。\n打击走私犯，保卫瓦利诺斯。

column5: And it's not like that?
column6: 难道不是那样吗？

column5: No, not at all!\nI spend most of my day standing around.\nCrime in Valinorth is almost non-existent.
column6: 不，完全不是！\n我一天大部分时间就是站着发呆。\n瓦利诺斯几乎没什么犯罪。

column5: Because the spirits have blessed us, right?
column6: 因为精灵祝福了我们，对吧？

column5: I guess that's one popular theory.\nBut to be honest, I don't buy it.\nSpirits can't change our nature.
column6: 我猜那是流行说法之一。\n但说实话，我不信。\n精灵改变不了我们的本性。

column5: Nature...?
column6: 本性……？

column5: Deep down inside, we're all evil.\nSome of us just manage it better than others.\nWe all have our impulses. It's about controlling them.
column6: 在我们内心深处，全都是邪恶的。\n只是有些人比别人更善于控制。\n我们都有冲动。关键在于克制。

column5: What an odd outlook.
column6: 真是古怪的看法。

column5: Hey, don't deny your impulses, Valessa.\nIf you had to steal to get by, you'd do it.\nValinorth is just special. Resources are everywhere.
column6: 嘿，别否认你的冲动，瓦莱莎。\n如果你得靠偷窃才能活下去，你也会做的。\n瓦利诺斯只是很特别。资源到处都是。

column5: Mazeo has been almost completely deforested.\nYou can't just go into the forest and find food.\nThere's not enough natural running water, either.
column6: 马泽奥的森林几乎被砍光了。\n你没法随便走进林子里就找到食物。\n天然活水也不够。

column5: See, I didn't know that...
column6: 你看，我根本不知道这些……

column5: I don't blame you.\nEveryone in Valinorth is happy.\nNobody is scraping by, you know?
column6: 我不怪你。\n瓦利诺斯每个人都很快乐。\n没人过得紧巴巴的，你知道吗？

column5: Imagine if food was scarce.\nThere'd be a lot more people breaking the law.\nStealing it, hurting others for it, you name it.
column6: 想象一下如果食物短缺。\n犯法的人会多得多。\n偷食物、为了食物伤害别人，什么都有。

column5: How do you know about all of this?
column6: 你怎么会知道这些的？

column5: I've been to Mazeo a couple of times.\nTrust me, the guards there have it {i}much{/i} harder.\nThey don't even know if they'll survive their shifts.
column6: 我去过马泽奥几次。\n相信我，那里的守卫要{i}难{/i}得多。\n他们连自己能不能活过一班岗都不知道。

column5: Oh, wow...
column6: 哦，天哪……

column5: So when I say the post here in Valinorth is boring?\nI'm not really complaining, to be honest.\nI'd much prefer boring work, to you know — dying.
column6: 所以当我说瓦利诺斯这儿的岗位很无聊？\n说实话，我不是在抱怨。\n比起——你懂的——死掉，我宁可干无聊的活。

column5: Damek returned to the surface with Gryz at his side.{w}\nThe older man took a deep breath, enjoying the fresh air.{w}\nIt was a little stuffy down there. But they could make do.
column6: 达梅克回到地面，格瑞兹就在他身旁。{w}\n那位年长的男人深吸一口气，享受着新鲜空气。{w}\n下面有点闷。但他们还能凑合。

column5: Digging tunnels underneath their own church.\nI guess it makes sense. Nobody really comes here.\nMazeo isn't exactly known for its pious people.
column6: 在他们自己的教堂下面挖隧道。\n我猜这说得通。反正没人会来这儿。\n马泽奥可不是以虔诚闻名的。

column5: Easy to get away with.\nThough I have to say, it's pretty ironic.\nThe Rebellion, settling in The Triumvirate's church.
column6: 很容易蒙混过去。\n不过我不得不说，这挺讽刺的。\n反抗军，安扎在三人执政团的教堂里。

column5: A bit poetic, isn't it?\nMaybe after this, we can settle in their castle.
column6: 有点诗意，不是吗？\n也许这之后，我们就能安扎进他们的城堡了。

column5: One step at a time. Let's not get carried away.\nI'll write them, and let them know what we've found.\nAfter all these years, I'm not sure how to feel.
column6: 一步一步来。别得意忘形。\n我会写信给他们，让他们知道我们发现了什么。\n这么多年过去了，我说不清自己是什么感受。

column5: Relieved, with a side of being terrified.\nAt least, that's how I feel about all of this.\nFinding another Spirit Idol. This changes everything.
column6: 如释重负，同时又怕得要命。\n至少，我对这一切的感觉就是这样。\n又找到一尊精灵灵像。这会改变一切。

column5: We always assumed {i}that{/i} was the idol. At the altar.\nIt was always so dim, we just thought that it was dying.\nBut it was receiving power from something deep underground.
column6: 我们一直以为祭坛上{i}那尊{/i}就是灵像。\n它总是那么黯淡，我们还以为它快消亡了。\n但它其实一直在从地底深处吸取力量。

column5: It's nice to know that the theories were correct.\nThis search was starting to feel like a lost cause.
column6: 知道那些推论是对的，真好。\n这场搜寻一度让人觉得是徒劳。

column5: The only lost cause is their pursuit of conquest.\nLet them know what you've found. Let's get things started.
column6: 唯一徒劳的，是他们追求征服的野心。\n让他们知道你的发现。我们开始行动吧。

column5: What are you planning, Damek?
column6: 你在谋划什么，达梅克？

column5: I'll let you know tomorrow, if everything goes well.\nI have to prepare for the arrival of our special guest.\nBut trust me, I've put a lot of thought into this plan.
column6: 如果一切顺利，我明天会告诉你。\n我得为那位特别客人的到来做准备。\n但相信我，这个计划我想了很久。

column5: You've earned my trust.
column6: 你已经赢得了我的信任。

column5: Gryz nods before leaving the church.{w}\nDamek, now alone, approaches the altar.{w}\nHe smiles as he places a hand upon it.
column6: 格瑞兹点点头，离开了教堂。{w}\n如今独自一人的达梅克走向祭坛。{w}\n他把手放上去时，露出了微笑。

column5: It won't be long until The Triumvirate sends their forces.\nIf I'm lucky, they might even come to see it for themselves.
column6: 用不了多久，三人执政团就会派出他们的军队。\n要是我运气好，他们甚至可能亲自来看一看。

column5: His smile turns into more of a sinister smirk.
column6: 他的微笑渐渐变成了一抹阴险的狞笑。

column5: Right now, they're busy with Valinorth.\nBut by the time they reroute, my army will be in place.\nWhen they set foot underground, we'll kill them all.
column6: 眼下，他们正忙着对付瓦利诺斯。\n但等他们改变路线时，我的军队已经就位。\n等他们踏入地下，我们就把他们全部杀光。

column5: Halin finally caught up with his master.{w}\nHe was slightly out of breath, having run a great distance.{w}\nBut his annoyance outweighed anything. He was lied to.
column6: 哈林终于追上了他的主人。{w}\n他跑了很远，微微有些气喘。{w}\n但恼怒压过了一切。他被骗了。

column5: Sovy, explain yourself immediately.\nYou told me to wait in the castle atrium.\nIf I did that, you would've left without me.
column6: 索维，马上给我解释清楚。\n你让我在城堡中庭等着。\n要是我真照做了，你就会丢下我自己走。

column5: Oh, did I really say that? I'm sorry.\nI must've gotten carried away with our prisoner.\nHow did your meeting with The Triumvirate go, Halin?
column6: 哦，我真的那么说了吗？抱歉。\n我一定是忙着处理我们的囚犯忘了。\n你和三人执政团的会面怎么样，哈林？

column5: They refused to tell me these \"secrets\".\nSomething about my loyalty not being strong enough.
column6: 他们拒绝告诉我那些“秘密”。\n说什么我的忠诚还不够坚定。

column5: Well look at it this way, Halin.\nThe mission we're going on is {i}very{/i} important.\nNo better way to prove your loyalty to the cause.
column6: 这么想吧，哈林。\n我们要执行的任务{i}非常{/i}重要。\n没有比这更好的机会来证明你对事业的忠诚了。

column5: I guess you're right.\nBut I don't like being left in the dark.
column6: 你说得大概没错。\n但我不喜欢被蒙在鼓里。

column5: Then you'll get along great with Shane.\nHe's been pestering me with questions all day.
column6: 那你会和肖恩相处得很融洽。\n他一整天都在拿问题烦我。

column5: I don't fraternize with prisoners.
column6: 我不和囚犯打交道。

column5: Whatever you say.
column6: 随你怎么说。

column5: Sovy walks away, laughing in a mocking fashion.{w}\nHalin and the prisoner slowly follow suit.
column6: 索维走开了，讥讽地笑着。{w}\n哈林和那名囚犯慢慢跟了上去。

column5: You know, we have a long boat ride ahead of us.\nMight not be a bad time to start \"fraternizing\".
column6: 你知道吗，我们前面还有很长一段水路。\n现在开始“打交道”也许不错。

column5: Did I stutter, Shane? Leave me be.
column6: 我结巴了吗，肖恩？别烦我。

column5: Oh, you think you're better than me, right?\nWell here's some food for thought, \"Apprentice\".\nYou're more a prisoner to The Triumvirate than I am.
column6: 哦，你觉得你比我高一等，是吧？\n那我给你点东西琢磨琢磨，“学徒”。\n你对三人执政团来说，比我更像囚犯。

column5: What did you just say...?
column6: 你刚才说什么……？

column5: Neither of us will know true freedom.\nWe're nothing but a means to an end.\nThey'll kill you the moment you disobey.
column6: 我们俩都尝不到真正的自由。\n我们不过是达成目的的工具。\n你一违抗命令，他们就会杀了你。

column5: We have no choice but to follow orders.\nThe difference is, you do this willingly.\nI have no idea why. You seem smart to me.
column6: 我们别无选择，只能听从命令。\n区别在于，你是自愿的。\n我真不明白为什么。你看起来挺聪明的。

column5: Whoa, this is amazing...!\nI can't believe something like this was so close.
column6: 哇，太惊人了……！\n真不敢相信这样的东西就在这么近的地方。

column5: And look at the Spirit Idol! That's so cool!\nEven if it's not lit up, it's still beautiful.
column6: 看那尊精灵灵像！太酷了！\n就算它没亮起来，也依然很美。

column5: Mylus said it went dark when [firstname] was born...?\nI can't believe all of that energy is inside of you.
column6: 迈勒斯说它是在[firstname]出生时暗下去的吗……？\n真不敢相信那么多能量都在你体内。

column5: Mylus said it went dark when [firstname] was born...?\nI can't believe all of that energy is inside of you.
column6: 迈勒斯说它是在[firstname]出生时暗下去的吗……？\n真不敢相信那么多能量都在你体内。

column5: They both look at me, as if they don't understand.{w}\nBut I guess that's fine. We don't really know what's happening.{w}\nI must've been given this power for a purpose. But what purpose?
column6: 她们都看着我，似乎并不明白。{w}\n不过我想没关系。我们其实也不知道发生了什么。{w}\n我被赋予这份力量一定有某种目的。可究竟是什么目的？

column5: Hey! Race you to the idol, Valessa!
column6: 嘿！比谁先到灵像那儿，瓦莱莎！

column5: He starts running like his life depends on it.{w}\nQuite the head start, if you ask me.
column6: 他拔腿就跑，像是性命攸关似的。{w}\n要我说，这抢跑可够早的。

column5: Hey, that's not fair!
column6: 嘿，这不公平！

column5: She quickly follows after him, closing the distance.{w}\nIt was nice to see their spirits lifted like this.{w}\nI might as well make the most of my time here.
column6: 她飞快地跟了上去，追近了距离。{w}\n看到他们这样兴致高涨，真好。{w}\n我也不妨好好利用在这里的时间。

column5: It appears that Mylus has people take care of this place.{w}\nThere's no other explanation for the grass being so short.{w}\nIf it was truly abandoned, it would be almost as tall as us.
column6: 看来迈勒斯让人打理着这个地方。{w}\n草这么短，没有别的解释。{w}\n如果这里真的荒废了，草几乎会长得跟我们一样高。

column5: I always knew that Mylus had people guard Sauleberg.\nBut I thought it was to keep the spirit idol safe.\nNow we know, it's so they don't find out it's dark.
column6: 我一直知道迈勒斯派人守卫着索尔伯格。\n但我以为那是为了保护精灵灵像。\n现在我们知道，是为了不让人发现它已经黯淡了。

column5: So we weren't the first ones that he told, then?\nThe guards must've known if they stood watch all day.\nI can't even think of anyone Mylus trusts that much.
column6: 那么，我们不是他告诉的第一批人？\n守卫们整天看守，肯定早就知道。\n我都想不出迈勒斯还这么信任谁。

column5: Well, we can't hide this from the people forever.\nIf we resettle Valinorth, they'll need to know.
column6: 我们不能永远把这件事瞒着民众。\n如果要重新迁回瓦利诺斯，他们就得知道。

column5: What!? No fair! How did you beat me...?
column6: 什么！？不公平！你怎么赢我的……？

column5: Even with a head start, you're no match for me.\nTime to throw in the towel. Stick to climbing trees.
column6: 就算抢跑，你也不是我的对手。\n认输吧。还是专心爬树去吧。

column5: Oh, so you want to have a climbing race?
column6: 哦，那你想比爬树咯？

column5: I'll pass, thanks.
column6: 我就不了，谢谢。

column5: Wait, why...?
column6: 等等，为什么……？

column5: A smart person doesn't pick a battle they know they'll lose.\nI'm surprised you challenged me Fortaime, you know how fast I am.
column6: 聪明人不会挑一场明知会输的仗打。\n我还真意外你敢挑战我，福泰姆，你又不是不知道我有多快。

column5: Are you calling me stupid!?
column6: 你是在说我笨吗！？

column5: No, I'd {i}never{/i} do that.
column6: 不，我{i}绝不会{/i}那么说。

column5: Anyway, isn't the spirit idol beautiful?
column6: 总之，这精灵灵像不美吗？

column5: That's putting it lightly.\nIt's one of the coolest things I've ever seen.\nWhen it's lit up, it must be incredible.
column6: 这说得太轻描淡写了。\n这是我这辈子见过最酷的东西之一。\n它亮起来的时候，一定美得惊人。

column5: Yeah, I'd pay almost any price to see that.\nBut don't worry Fortaime, I'm sure there's something we can do.\nIf we all work together, we can make that idol shine again.
column6: 是啊，为了看到那个，我几乎愿意付出任何代价。\n但别担心，福泰姆，我相信总有办法。\n如果我们齐心协力，就能让那尊灵像重新闪耀。

column5: So this is it. The idol that gave me its power.{w}\nAgainst my will, I was chosen for this greater destiny.{w}\nThe last Seer of Valinorth. Perhaps, the savior of Alestia.
column6: 就是它了。赋予我力量的灵像。{w}\n违背我的意愿，我被选中去承担这份更伟大的命运。{w}\n瓦利诺斯最后的先知。也许，还是阿莱斯蒂亚的救世主。

column5: So this is it. The idol that gave me its power.{w}\nAgainst my will, I was chosen for this greater destiny.{w}\nThe last Seeress of Valinorth. Perhaps, the savior of Alestia.
column6: 就是它了。赋予我力量的灵像。{w}\n违背我的意愿，我被选中去承担这份更伟大的命运。{w}\n瓦利诺斯最后的女先知。也许，还是阿莱斯蒂亚的救世主。

column5: I can't believe we've lost our connection with the spirits.\nThere must be some way to get it back, right...?
column6: 真不敢相信，我们失去了与精灵的联系。\n总有办法恢复的吧，对吧……？

column5: Are you sure we lost it, though?\nIt's still here, just inside of [firstname].
column6: 可你确定我们失去了吗？\n它还在，就在[firstname]体内。

column5: Are you sure we lost it, though?\nIt's still here, just inside of [firstname].
column6: 可你确定我们失去了吗？\n它还在，就在[firstname]体内。

column5: I'm pretty sure it's not that simple.\nThis idol has roots that reach all across Valinorth.\nAs far as I know, [firstname] doesn't have any roots.
column6: 我很确定没那么简单。\n这尊灵像的根系遍布整个瓦利诺斯。\n据我所知，[firstname]可没有根。

column5: I'm pretty sure it's not that simple.\nThis idol has roots that reach all across Valinorth.\nAs far as I know, [firstname] doesn't have any roots.
column6: 我很确定没那么简单。\n这尊灵像的根系遍布整个瓦利诺斯。\n据我所知，[firstname]可没有根。

column5: Well, maybe there's a way to put the energy back.\nYou know, after we've taken down The Triumvirate...?
column6: 也许有办法把能量还回去。\n你知道，等我们扳倒三人执政团之后……？

column5: Yeah, that's what I was thinking.\nMaybe this is only temporary, and they'll come back.\n[firstname] won't need the power after we've won, right?
column6: 是啊，我也是这么想的。\n也许这只是暂时的，它们会回来的。\n我们赢了之后，[firstname]就不需要这份力量了，对吧？

column5: Yeah, that's what I was thinking.\nMaybe this is only temporary, and they'll come back.\n[firstname] won't need the power after we've won, right?
column6: 是啊，我也是这么想的。\n也许这只是暂时的，它们会回来的。\n我们赢了之后，[firstname]就不需要这份力量了，对吧？

column5: We look at each other, and smile.{w}\nThere had to be a way to reconnect Valinorth with the spirits.{w}\nWe had a long journey ahead of us, and plenty of time to learn how.
column6: 我们相视而笑。{w}\n一定有办法让瓦利诺斯重新与精灵相连。{w}\n前路漫长，我们有充足的时间去弄清楚。

column5: It looks like these bridges lead to The Outlook.{w}\nIt's technically the exit to the rest of Alestia.{w}\nA long mountain trail takes you to the mainland.
column6: 这些桥似乎通向观景台。{w}\n严格来说，那是通往阿莱斯蒂亚其他地区的出口。{w}\n一条漫长的山道会把你带到大陆。

column5: The trail from Peregrino is probably safer, though.{w}\nThose bridges look like they could break at any second.{w}\nEspecially if they've been neglected for over twenty years.
column6: 不过，从佩雷格里诺来的那条路大概更安全。{w}\n那些桥看着随时都可能断。{w}\n尤其是它们已经被荒废了二十多年的话。

column5: So this is it. The idol that gave me its power.{w}\nAgainst my will, I was chosen for this greater destiny.{w}\nThe last Seer of Valinorth. Perhaps, the savior of Alestia.
column6: 就是它了。赋予我力量的灵像。{w}\n违背我的意愿，我被选中去承担这份更伟大的命运。{w}\n瓦利诺斯最后的先知。也许，还是阿莱斯蒂亚的救世主。

column5: So this is it. The idol that gave me its power.{w}\nAgainst my will, I was chosen for this greater destiny.{w}\nThe last Seeress of Valinorth. Perhaps, the savior of Alestia.
column6: 就是它了。赋予我力量的灵像。{w}\n违背我的意愿，我被选中去承担这份更伟大的命运。{w}\n瓦利诺斯最后的女先知。也许，还是阿莱斯蒂亚的救世主。

column5: I can't believe we've lost our connection with the spirits.\nThere must be some way to get it back, right...?
column6: 真不敢相信，我们失去了与精灵的联系。\n总有办法恢复的吧，对吧……？

column5: Are you sure we lost it, though?\nIt's still here, just inside of [firstname].
column6: 可你确定我们失去了吗？\n它还在，就在[firstname]体内。

column5: Are you sure we lost it, though?\nIt's still here, just inside of [firstname].
column6: 可你确定我们失去了吗？\n它还在，就在[firstname]体内。

column5: I'm pretty sure it's not that simple.\nThis idol has roots that reach all across Valinorth.\nAs far as I know, [firstname] doesn't have any roots.
column6: 我很确定没那么简单。\n这尊灵像的根系遍布整个瓦利诺斯。\n据我所知，[firstname]可没有根。

column5: I'm pretty sure it's not that simple.\nThis idol has roots that reach all across Valinorth.\nAs far as I know, [firstname] doesn't have any roots.
column6: 我很确定没那么简单。\n这尊灵像的根系遍布整个瓦利诺斯。\n据我所知，[firstname]可没有根。

column5: Well, maybe there's a way to put the energy back.\nYou know, after we've taken down The Triumvirate...?
column6: 也许有办法把能量还回去。\n你知道，等我们扳倒三人执政团之后……？

column5: Yeah, that's what I was thinking.\nMaybe this is only temporary, and they'll come back.\n[firstname] won't need the power after we've won, right?
column6: 是啊，我也是这么想的。\n也许这只是暂时的，它们会回来的。\n我们赢了之后，[firstname]就不需要这份力量了，对吧？

column5: Yeah, that's what I was thinking.\nMaybe this is only temporary, and they'll come back.\n[firstname] won't need the power after we've won, right?
column6: 是啊，我也是这么想的。\n也许这只是暂时的，它们会回来的。\n我们赢了之后，[firstname]就不需要这份力量了，对吧？

column5: We look at each other, and smile.{w}\nThere had to be a way to reconnect Valinorth with the spirits.{w}\nWe had a long journey ahead of us, and plenty of time to learn how.
column6: 我们相视而笑。{w}\n一定有办法让瓦利诺斯重新与精灵相连。{w}\n前路漫长，我们有充足的时间去弄清楚。

column5: After a lengthy trek through the forest, we arrive at Peregrino.{w}\nThe scent of ale and the aged wood of the tavern permeate the air.{w}\nZamira lets out a sigh of relief, having finally achieved his goal.
column6: 在森林里长途跋涉之后，我们抵达了佩雷格里诺。{w}\n麦酒的香气和酒馆陈年木料的气息弥漫在空气中。{w}\n终于达成目标的扎米拉松了一口气。

column5: Well, looks like we're finally here.\nIt wasn't that bad, was it...?
column6: 好了，看来我们终于到了。\n也没那么糟，对吧……？

column5: Not as bad as I thought it'd be!
column6: 没我想的那么糟！

column5: My legs are little sore, but I'll manage.\nI know we're far from home, but this still feels like \"Valinorth\".\nI guess maybe I expected something a little different.
column6: 我的腿有点酸，但还撑得住。\n我知道我们离家很远，但这里感觉还是像“瓦利诺斯”。\n也许我只是期待了点不一样的东西。

column5: Just wait until you see The Outlook, Valessa!
column6: 等你看到观景台就知道了，瓦莱莎！

column5: The Outlook...?
column6: 观景台……？

column5: Yeah, you can almost see the entirety of Alestia.\nAs soon as there's no trees in the way, you'll be amazed.\nIt's easy to forget we're on top of the highest mountains.
column6: 是啊，你几乎能看见整个阿莱斯蒂亚。\n只要没有树挡着，你一定会惊叹。\n很容易忘记我们正身处最高的群山之巅。

column5: So we're not surrounded by trees the entire way to Mazeo?
column6: 所以去马泽奥的路上不会一直都被树包围？

column5: Absolutely not. \nEven aside from the deforesting, trees are scarce.\nIt makes for a beautiful view, I'm sure you'll love it.
column6: 绝对不会。 \n就算不谈滥伐的事，那里的树也很稀少。\n那会是很美的景色，我相信你会喜欢的。

column5: The tone of his voice implied that he wouldn't be going with us.{w}\nIf he's seen it before, then I doubt that staying behind was a big deal.{w}\nBut for some reason, Fortaime and Valessa seem a bit upset at hearing this.
column6: 他的语气暗示他不会和我们一起去。{w}\n如果他以前见过，那我想留下来也没什么大不了。{w}\n但不知为何，福泰姆和瓦莱莎听到后似乎有些失落。

column5: Right, I guess you're on your own schedule now.\nYou only had to bring us to Peregrino.
column6: 也是，我猜你现在有自己的安排。\n你只需要把我们带到佩雷格里诺。

column5: I'm not about to ditch you, though!\nI'll head inside, feel free to follow along.\nIt won't be too hard to find Pro. Trust me.
column6: 不过我可不打算撂下你们！\n我先进去，你们随意跟来。\n找到普洛不会太难。相信我。

column5: He leaves our side, and starts walking into the tavern.{w}\nWe exchange glances, seeming a little hesitant.
column6: 他离开我们身边，朝酒馆里走去。{w}\n我们交换了个眼神，显得有些犹豫。

column5: Well, I guess this is it.\nAs soon as we meet with Pro, we're off to Mazeo.
column6: 好了，我想就是现在了。\n一见完普洛，我们就要出发去马泽奥。

column5: Wait, did you say Pro?
column6: 等等，你刚说普洛？

column5: We're all startled by the sudden intrusion.{w}\nBut to me, this voice is immediately recognizable. Ulric...?
column6: 我们都被这突如其来的插话吓了一跳。{w}\n但对我来说，这声音立刻就认出来了。乌尔里克……？

column5: What!? Who's there?
column6: 什么！？谁在那儿？

column5: He lets out a soft laugh as he approaches us.{w}\nAfter looking me up and down, a wide smile appears on his face.{w}\nI forgot we haven't actually met. It's the blade on my back he notices.
column6: 他走近我们，轻轻笑了一声。{w}\n上下打量我之后，他脸上绽开一个大大的笑容。{w}\n我忘了我们其实没见过面。他注意到的是我背上的那把剑。

column5: Well what do you know. It's {i}you{/i}.\nKind of makes my job a whole lot easier.
column6: 哎呀，没想到。是{i}你{/i}啊。\n这倒让我的活儿轻松多了。

column5: Wait, you know us?
column6: 等等，你认识我们？

column5: Just [firstname].
column6: 只认识[firstname]。

column5: Just [firstname].
column6: 只认识[firstname]。

column5: Then you must be—
column6: 那你一定是——

column5: Ulric! From the vision...!
column6: 乌尔里克！幻象里的那个……！

column5: Excuse me...?
column6: 什么……？

column5: Yeah! You were in the vision that [firstname] had last night.
column6: 对！你在[firstname]昨晚看到的幻象里。

column5: Yeah! You were in the vision that [firstname] had last night.
column6: 对！你在[firstname]昨晚看到的幻象里。

column5: Huh. Haven't even met and I'm already in your dreams?\nThat {i}has{/i} to be some kind of new personal record.
column6: 哈。还没见面我就已经进你梦里了？\n这{i}绝对{/i}是我的新纪录了。

column5: He cracks another smile. Is that an attempt at flirtation?{w}\nIf it was, it wouldn't go anywhere. Fortaime promptly interrupts.
column6: 他又咧嘴一笑。这是在试探着调情吗？{w}\n就算是，也不会有什么结果。福泰姆立刻打断了他。

column5: He said you died, Ulric...\nSomething about a man named Sovy.
column6: 他说你死了，乌尔里克……\n好像和一个叫索维的人有关。

column5: She said you died, Ulric...\nSomething about a man named Sovy.
column6: 她说你死了，乌尔里克……\n好像和一个叫索维的人有关。

column5: His ears perk up as he hears the name Sovy.{w}\nBut he seems to find something comedic about Fortaime's words.{w}\nClapping his hands together, simply once, he smirks at the three of us.
column6: 听到索维这个名字，他竖起了耳朵。{w}\n但福泰姆的话似乎让他觉得有些好笑。{w}\n他双手一拍，只拍了一下，便朝我们三人露出了坏笑。

column5: You sure are good at first impressions, little one.
column6: 你还真是会给人留下第一印象啊，小家伙。

column5: I'm not little!
column6: 我才不是小家伙！

column5: It seems that nobody jumps to Fortaime's defense.
column6: 似乎没人替福泰姆说话。

column5: Is he telling the truth, [firstname]?
column6: 他说的是真的吗，[firstname]？

column5: Is he telling the truth, [firstname]?
column6: 他说的是真的吗，[firstname]？

column5: How exciting.\nYou'll have to tell me more once we grab Pro.\nAfter that, we're going to evacuate Valinorth.
column6: 真让人兴奋。\n等我们找到普洛，你可得跟我多说点。\n那之后，我们要去疏散瓦利诺斯。

column5: Well I guess I'll have to loosen you up a little.\nMaybe we'll grab a drink while we meet up with Pro.\nAfter that, we have to go evacuate Valinorth — and quick.
column6: 看来我得让你放松一点才行。\n也许见到普洛的时候我们喝一杯。\n那之后，我们得去疏散瓦利诺斯——而且要快。

column5: It seems like he's able to piece things together.{w}\nThe vision of his death — and Sovy — was Valinorth's destruction.{w}\nHe wastes no time in suggesting our immediate course of action.
column6: 看来他能把线索串起来。{w}\n他死亡的幻象——还有索维——意味着瓦利诺斯的毁灭。{w}\n他毫不耽搁地提出我们该立刻采取的行动。

column5: Actually, Mylus is taking care of that.\nThe village is gathering for a celebration tonight.\nThe perfect time to group up and escape, right?
column6: 其实，迈勒斯正在处理这件事。\n今晚全村要聚在一起庆祝。\n正是集合撤离的绝佳时机，对吧？

column5: Really? I'm starting to wonder why I'm even here.\nEither way, Pro and I will take you to Damek.\nGlad to hear this vision of yours won't come to pass.
column6: 真的？我都开始怀疑我来这儿干什么了。\n不管怎样，我和普洛会带你们去见达梅克。\n很高兴听说你们这个幻象不会成真。

column5: That much is true. He'd avoid Valinorth entirely.{w}\nToo bad the attack on Valinorth wasn't something we could avoid.
column6: 这话没错。他会完全避开瓦利诺斯。{w}\n可惜对瓦利诺斯的袭击是我们避不开的。

column5: Shall we get things started...?\nUnless you want to talk more, I'm up for that too.
column6: 我们开始吧……？\n除非你还想再聊聊，我也奉陪。

column5: I can't tell if he's being genuine or sarcastic.{w}\nIt's hard to get a read on this man, and that's odd.{w}\nHis resolve in last night's vision, his demeanor, was clear.
column6: 我分不清他是真心还是在讽刺。{w}\n这个人很难看透，而这很奇怪。{w}\n昨晚幻象中他的决心，他的神态，都很清晰。

column5: I feel like, even though we barely talked, we're on the same page.{w}\nHe seems to know why we're here, where we're going, and what we need to do.{w}\nThat makes things a bit easier. Endless planning would be tedious.
column6: 我觉得，尽管我们几乎没说过话，却很有默契。{w}\n他似乎知道我们为什么来、要去哪里、需要做什么。{w}\n这让事情简单了些。无休止的盘算会很乏味。

column5: Whenever you're ready, [firstname].\nSeems like we have a lot ahead of us.
column6: 你准备好了随时说，[firstname]。\n看来我们前头还有很多事。

column5: Whenever you're ready, [firstname].\nSeems like we have a lot ahead of us.
column6: 你准备好了随时说，[firstname]。\n看来我们前头还有很多事。

column5: We all look at each other before nodding.{w}\nIt seems like everyone else is following my lead.{w}\nI could probe Ulric for information, or head right inside.
column6: 我们互相看了看，然后点头。{w}\n似乎其他人都听我指挥。{w}\n我可以向乌尔里克打探消息，或者直接进去。

column5: Ulric has now permanently joined your party.
column6: 乌尔里克已永久加入你的队伍。

column5: The tavern looks old, but well taken care of.{w}\nIf it wasn't given frequent care, it would be dilapidated.{w}\nThe love given to this place by the owner clearly shines through.
column6: 酒馆看起来老旧，但打理得很好。{w}\n如果不是经常照料，它早就破败了。{w}\n店主对这地方倾注的爱意显而易见。

column5: It's a lot taller than I thought it'd be.
column6: 比我想象的高多了。

column5: Well it doubles as a sort of \"hotel\".\nI'm assuming the topmost floors are private rooms.
column6: 它同时也兼作某种“旅馆”。\n我猜最上面几层是客房。

column5: Oh, really? That's cool.\nMaybe we can rest before we leave.
column6: 哦，真的？那不错。\n也许我们走之前能休息一下。

column5: If we have the time, perhaps we can.\nIt might be nice to explore this place in person.\nI've read about it, and heard lots of stories.
column6: 如果有时间，或许可以。\n亲自探索这个地方应该不错。\n我读到过关于它的东西，也听过很多故事。

column5: What kind of stories...?
column6: 什么样的故事……？

column5: If they're true — you'll see for yourself.
column6: 如果它们是真的——你自己就会看到了。

column5: The trees stretch up as high as the eye can see.{w}\nIt's still bright out, so sun pierces through the canopy.{w}\nThankfully, it's not too overwhelming. It simply looks beautiful.
column6: 树木高耸入云，一眼望不到顶。{w}\n天色还亮，阳光穿透树冠洒下来。{w}\n幸好还不算太刺眼。只是看着很美。

column5: Wow, look at all these trees...!\nThey'd be perfect for climbing!\nMind if I take a quick detour?
column6: 哇，看看这些树……！\n简直太适合攀爬了！\n介意我稍微绕个道吗？

column5: Come on, Fortaime. We don't have time.\nAren't there more important matters at hand?
column6: 算了吧，福泰姆。我们没时间。\n眼下没有更重要的事吗？

column5: If I don't practice, how will I ever climb The Grand Tree!?\nYou gotta give me some time every once in a while, Valessa.
column6: 要是不练习，我怎么可能爬得上巨树！？\n你偶尔也得给我点时间啊，瓦莱莎。

column5: Perhaps. But not now.\nI don't have time to treat any injuries.
column6: 也许吧。但不是现在。\n我可没时间给你治伤。

column5: I can treat them myself!
column6: 我自己能治！

column5: Really? You sure fooled me.
column6: 是吗？你倒是骗到我了。

column5: I'm assuming in the dark, this helps people find Peregrino.{w}\nHowever, right now, it seems to serve no real purpose.{w}\nTo come here during the day, you'd have to know exactly where it was.
column6: 我猜在黑暗中，这东西能帮人找到佩雷格里诺。{w}\n不过眼下，它似乎没什么实际用处。{w}\n白天来这里，你得确切知道它在哪儿才行。

column5: I'm sure glad we had Zamira here to guide us.\nWithout him, I'm pretty sure we'd have gotten lost.
column6: 还好有扎米拉在这儿给我们带路。\n没他的话，我们肯定会迷路。

column5: Let's not think about that, alright?\nI'm just thankful we have such great friends.\nThey're all risking a lot for us, you know?
column6: 别想那个了，好吗？\n我只庆幸我们有这么好的朋友。\n你知道，他们都在为我们冒很大的风险。

column5: True. But honestly, we're risking even more.\nWhen this is all over, we could go down in history.\nIt makes sense that they'd want to be remembered too.
column6: 没错。但说实话，我们冒的风险更大。\n等这一切结束，我们可能会名留青史。\n他们也想被记住，这也说得通。

column5: Remembered...?\nDo you mean they're helping us for glory?\nI'd like to think that they were just being nice.
column6: 被记住……？\n你是说他们帮我们是为了荣耀？\n我倒愿意相信他们只是出于好心。

column5: I wish that's how people worked.\nYou really think Zamira did this for free?\nHe must be receiving some kind of payment.
column6: 我倒希望人都是那样的。\n你真觉得扎米拉是白帮忙的？\n他肯定收了某种报酬。

column5: Aren't we going on this journey for \"free\"?\nThere's no promise of fame, money, {i}or{/i} glory.
column6: 我们不也是“免费”踏上这趟旅程的吗？\n既没有名声、金钱，也{i}没有{/i}荣耀的承诺。

column5: But the possibility can be even more appealing.\nEither way, {i}any{/i} help we can get is good.\nNo need to dig into people's motives, Valessa.
column6: 但那种可能性反而更诱人。\n不管怎样，能得到{i}任何{/i}帮助都是好事。\n没必要深究别人的动机，瓦莱莎。

column5: You're the one that did it though...
column6: 可刚才那么说的人是你……

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: Absolutely. I'd recognize that thing anywhere.\nI'm surprised you have it out in the open like that.\nWe went through such great lengths to hide it.
column6: 当然。那东西我一眼就能认出来。\n我很意外你竟然就那样大喇喇地露在外面。\n我们当年可是费尽心思才把它藏起来。

column5: About The Blade of Exodus? It's extraordinary.\nI have no idea where it came from, or the full range of its power.\nIt can repurpose life into an energy that serves the wielder.
column6: 是说出流亡之刃吗？它非同凡响。\n我不知道它从何而来，也不知道它力量的全部范围。\n它能把生命转化为供持有者驱使的能量。

column5: That gear at the base can spin, which should be impossible.\nIt's almost like some parts of the blade exist in a different world.\nI'm starting to think that's the case. Where else would it store all that power?
column6: 底部那个齿轮能转动，这按理说是不可能的。\n就好像剑的某些部分存在于另一个世界。\n我开始觉得真是这样。不然它把那么多力量储存在哪儿？

column5: It's practically cheating. Whoever wields it has infinite power.\nI don't think of The Triumvirate as Gods. They were just abusing this weapon.\nNow that they don't have it — taking them down should be child's play.
column6: 这简直就是作弊。谁持有它，谁就有无穷的力量。\n我不把三人执政团当神看。他们不过是滥用这件武器罢了。\n如今他们没了它——扳倒他们应该轻而易举。

column5: I have no idea, and I don't think we'll ever find out.\nIt must tap into a person's spirit before it enters the spirit realm.\nThat's the only non-physical part of us that could be considered energy.
column6: 我毫无头绪，也不觉得我们会有弄明白的一天。\n它一定是在一个人的灵进入灵界之前将其抽取。\n那是我们身上唯一能被视作能量的非物质部分。

column5: I'm assuming they've always had it. It's how they came to power.\nSome people seem to think they used the blade to create our entire world.\nNot many people know about it, though — and they see The Triumvirate as Gods.
column6: 我猜他们一直都有它。他们就是靠它掌权的。\n有些人似乎认为他们用那把剑创造了我们的整个世界。\n不过知道这件事的人不多——而且他们把三人执政团奉为神明。

column5: They really aren't. They're just men who came upon a greater power.\nAnd now {i}we{/i} have that greater power. We can rule Alestia far better than them.\nI think we should destroy that blade after we win. It's a tool of pure corruption.
column6: 他们根本不是神。他们只是撞上了更强大力量的凡人。\n而现在{i}我们{/i}拥有了那更强大的力量。我们能比他们更好地统治阿莱斯蒂亚。\n我觉得我们赢了之后应该毁掉那把剑。它是纯粹腐败的产物。

column5: It wasn't too long ago. Maybe half a year. The Rebellion planned an attack.\nOur previous leader planned it down to even the {i}smallest{/i} detail.\nSteal the blade, map out their castle — and pave way for our future liberation.
column6: 不算太久，大概半年前。反抗军策划了一次袭击。\n我们之前的那位领袖把它计划到了{i}最细微{/i}的细节。\n偷走那把剑，摸清他们城堡的地形——为我们未来的解放铺路。

column5: I'll be honest. He knew he was going to die. He used his final moments to get the blade.\nSome people think it's a little fishy. How could we win so easily? Did they let us win?\nI don't think it's that deep. They just didn't expect our leader to effectively commit suicide.
column6: 老实说，他知道自己会死。他用最后的时刻拿到了那把剑。\n有些人觉得有点蹊跷。我们怎么能赢得这么容易？是他们故意放水吗？\n我觉得没那么复杂。他们只是没料到我方领袖会等同于自杀。

column5: I was. Change the subject.
column6: 我确实会。换个话题吧。

column5: I'm sure you won't. I don't think any of us will.\nThe scope of his planning went farther than I could've imagined.\nBeing The Elder of Valinorth, he planned every aspect of your involvement.
column6: 我相信你不会。我觉得我们谁都不会。\n他谋划的规模远超我的想象。\n身为瓦利诺斯的长老，他把你参与的每个环节都计划好了。

column5: I guess breaking Valinorth's non-partisan stance made perfect sense to him.\nEvery little piece was in place. The liberation of Alestia was finally attainable.\nI just hope that you're everything he thought you'd be. Wielding that blade isn't easy.
column6: 我猜打破瓦利诺斯的中立立场，在他看来完全合理。\n每一小块拼图都各就各位。阿莱斯蒂亚的解放终于触手可及。\n我只希望你能如他所想的那般。挥舞那把剑可不容易。

column5: He already is, and I'm happy to serve him. Things are going swimmingly.\nIt helps that he was one of the founding members of The Rebellion, too.\nAt that point, though; he was too young to lead. Things are different now.
column6: 他已经是了，我很乐意为他效力。一切进展顺利。\n而且他也是反抗军的创始成员之一，这也有帮助。\n不过那时候他还太年轻，不能领导。现在情况不同了。

column5: He's done a fine job of honoring our leader's legacy, and guiding us to victory.\nHe had to make a few hard decisions, but I trust his judgment without question.\nEverything is going according to plan. Our final assault is all we need.
column6: 他很好地继承了我们领袖的遗志，引领我们走向胜利。\n他不得不做出几个艰难的决定，但我无条件信任他的判断。\n一切都在按计划进行。我们只差最后一场进攻。

column5: Wait — he used The Blade of Exodus on me? That's impossible.\nThere's no way he'd be able to wield it. You're the only one.\nEven Damek nearly died the first time he touched it.
column6: 等等——他用流亡之刃对我施了法？这不可能。\n他绝不可能驾驭它。你是唯一能做到的人。\n就连达梅克第一次碰它时都差点死掉。

column5: I'm still surprised though, he had a small vision when he did.\nPerhaps he has some spiritual energy inside of him...\nEither way — hopefully I went out in a blaze of glory.
column6: 不过我还是很惊讶，他那样做时看到了一个小幻象。\n也许他体内也有某种精灵之力……\n不管怎样——但愿我是轰轰烈烈地死去的。

column5: Yeah, that sounds like me. I wouldn't have it any other way.\nI'm just thankful that this vision won't come to pass. I have a lot of life left in me.\nThat makes me wonder, though — what was the purpose of seeing something like that?
column6: 是啊，那听起来像我。我也不想以别的方式死去。\n我只庆幸这个幻象不会成真。我还有很多日子要活。\n不过这让我好奇——看到那样的东西，究竟是为了什么？

column5: I can understand a vision of Valinorth being attacked. But seeing me, and watching me die?\nWe've never even met. How is it possible to know what I look like, and how I act?\nI know the spirits give visions of the future, but that's so specific; and it won't happen.
column6: 我能理解看到瓦利诺斯遭袭的幻象。但看到我，亲眼看着我死？\n我们甚至从未见过面。怎么可能知道我的长相和举止？\n我知道精灵会赐予未来的幻象，但那也太具体了；而且它不会发生。

column5: Sovy is an incredibly strong adversary, even without the blade.\nBut if he's able to wield it? We better make sure it never enters his hands.\nHis strength — coupled with that blade? I don't scare easily, but that's terrifying.
column6: 索维是个强得可怕的对手，就算没有那把剑也一样。\n但如果他能驾驭它呢？我们最好确保它永远不落进他手里。\n他的力量——再加上那把剑？我不容易害怕，但那确实很可怕。

column5: There's no way he should be able to. I imagine even {i}you're{/i} having trouble.\nIt's not meant for just anybody to wield. You need an incredible spiritual connection.\nDamek might have a small one, but Sovy? A man like that has {i}no{/i} connection to the spirits.
column6: 他绝不可能做到。我猜就连{i}你{/i}驾驭起来也很吃力。\n它不是随便什么人都能用的。你需要与精灵有非同寻常的联结。\n达梅克或许有一点，但索维？那样的人与精灵{i}毫无{/i}联结。

column5: Hard to say. That depends on your ability to wield it.\nThe Triumvirate had that blade for an eternity. You don't have that much time.\nNot to put too much pressure on your shoulders. It's just the truth.
column6: 很难说。那取决于你驾驭它的能力。\n三人执政团持有那把剑过了漫长的岁月。你没有那么多时间。\n不是想给你太多压力。只是事实如此。

column5: Yeah, but you also saw me die, right?\nThese visions aren't as reliable as I've been led to believe.\nRather than seeing the future, it's almost like it shows you what to {i}avoid{/i}.
column6: 是啊，但你也看到我死了，对吧？\n这些幻象并不像我听说的那么可靠。\n与其说是预见未来，倒不如说它是在告诉你该{i}避开{/i}什么。

column5: Too bad we can't avoid what's coming to Valinorth.\nWhen Damek touched the blade, he saw Valinorth fall, and The Rebellion win.\nIt seems like he's embracing what he saw. Good thing you're not, or else I'd be dead.
column6: 可惜我们避不开降临瓦利诺斯的事。\n达梅克碰那把剑时，他看见瓦利诺斯陷落，反抗军获胜。\n看来他接受了所看到的一切。幸好你没有，否则我就死定了。

column5: You mean how do I feel without our most valuable assets? Pretty terrible.\nWithout visions to guide us, and the power of that blade, we'd be dead.\nThere's no way we could take them down through conventional means.
column6: 你是说失去我们最宝贵的资产后我感觉如何？糟透了。\n没有幻象指引我们，没有那把剑的力量，我们早就死了。\n我们绝不可能用常规手段扳倒他们。

column5: However — at the moment, everything is in our favor. Everything.\nWe just need to be careful. Do {i}not{/i} let The Triumvirate or Sovy take that blade back.\nIf we can do that, victory is as good as ours. A new future will rise to greet Alestia.
column6: 不过——眼下，一切都有利于我们。一切。\n我们只需小心行事。{i}千万不要{/i}让三人执政团或索维夺回那把剑。\n只要做到这点，胜利就等同于是我们的。一个崭新的未来将迎向阿莱斯蒂亚。

column5: Scary is an understatement. But I've never been more certain of our victory.\nDamek is pretty excited to meet you, actually. You're going to help us win this war.
column6: 说可怕都太轻了。但我从没像现在这样笃定我们会胜利。\n其实达梅克很期待见到你。你会帮我们打赢这场战争。

column5: I'm fully aware of that. It'll take some training to get used to it.\nWhen we get to Mazeo, Damek will place you under a strict training regiment.\nYou need to get as much practice as possible before we launch our attack.
column6: 我很清楚这一点。得经过一些训练才能适应。\n到了马泽奥，达梅克会让你接受严格的训练。\n在我们发动进攻之前，你需要尽可能多练习。

column5: Of course, and I'm glad you look at it that way.\nPractice makes perfect. We can't expect you to use it immediately.\nJust do your best to be careful. You know what that thing is capable of.
column6: 当然，很高兴你能这么想。\n熟能生巧。我们不会指望你立刻就能用。\n尽力小心就好。你知道那东西有多大能耐。

column5: I'll pass, thanks.
column6: 我就不了，谢谢。

column5: Damek was able to use it, only for a brief second.\nAny longer than that, and he would've died.\nI think this one rests on your shoulders alone.
column6: 达梅克能用它，但也只有短短一瞬。\n再多哪怕一会儿，他就会死。\n我觉得这件事只能落在你一个人肩上了。

column5: And yet, here we are.\nLet's just go with the flow.\nNo use fighting what's set in stone.
column6: 可我们终究还是走到了这一步。\n就顺其自然吧。\n跟注定的事较劲也没用。

column5: Good. Fighting your calling is never the right idea.\nJust embrace it, and let's do great things together.\nYou'll make it out of this as a hero, you know.
column6: 很好。抗拒自己的使命从来都不是明智之举。\n坦然接受它，让我们一起成就伟业。\n你知道，你会以英雄的身份走出这一切。

column5: Well, The Rebellion was formed around twenty years ago.\nSurvivors of The Occupation banded together, and sought justice.\nAdults trained orphaned children, to create the perfect soldiers.
column6: 反抗军大约是在二十年前成立的。\n占领的幸存者聚集到一起，寻求正义。\n成年人训练失去双亲的孩子，以打造完美的士兵。

column5: A long time has passed, and now the children are old enough to fight.\nThat, and they've been perfectly trained. Almost their only purpose.\nDamek was one of these children. The previous leader raised him as his own.
column6: 很久过去了，如今那些孩子已经长大到可以战斗了。\n而且他们受过完美的训练。那几乎是他们唯一的用途。\n达梅克就是这些孩子中的一个。前任领袖把他当作亲生儿子养大。

column5: Obviously I'm a little older. I wasn't a victim of The Occupation.\nWhen it happened, I was just arriving in Mazeo to sell my sword arm.\nI moved here from Alarinthia as soon as I had the chance.
column6: 显然我年纪大一些。我不是占领的受害者。\n那件事发生时，我刚抵达马泽奥，准备当佣兵卖命。\n一有机会我就从阿拉林西亚搬到了这里。

column5: Imagine wanting to get a new start, and arriving in the middle of a war zone.\nThat's pretty much what happened. So I did what anybody else would do...\nI joined the winning side — The Triumvirate — with the hopes of making money.
column6: 想象一下，你本想开始新生活，结果抵达的却是战区中央。\n差不多就是这样。于是我做了任何人都会做的事……\n我加入了赢的那一方——三人执政团——想着能赚点钱。

column5: It was going well, but then I realized they were killing children.\nI turned on them as quickly as I joined them, fighting for Mazeo. \nI was one of the first rebels — got to watch Damek grow up first-hand.
column6: 一开始挺顺利，但后来我意识到他们在屠杀孩子。\n我背叛他们的速度和我加入他们一样快，转而替马泽奥而战。 \n我是最早的反抗者之一——亲眼看着达梅克长大。

column5: That's purely subjective, but I happen to think you're right.\nThe Triumvirate needs to be taken down, or held accountable for what they did.\nLeaders should never get a free pass to commit atrocities. Never.
column6: 这纯粹是主观看法，不过我恰好觉得你说得对。\n三人执政团必须被扳倒，或为他们的所作所为负责。\n领袖绝不该被免于为暴行负责。绝不。

column5: I'm sure there's been insurrections in the past. There must've been.\nBut the thing about us — is that we have The Blade of Exodus. Our victory.
column6: 我相信过去一定有过起义。肯定有。\n但我们不同的一点——是我们拥有流亡之刃。我们的胜利。

column5: Look, I realized the error of my ways, and did everything to make amends.\nWe can't say the same about The Triumvirate. They've chosen tyranny.\nYou can be mad at me all you want, but that's old news. A lifetime ago.
column6: 听着，我认识到了自己的错误，并竭尽全力弥补。\n三人执政团就不能这么说了。他们选择了暴政。\n你尽管生我的气，但那都是陈年旧事了。恍如隔世。

column5: Glad to know we think alike. Most people get upset when I tell them.\nThe most important thing, is that I'm a changed man. Our enemy is not.\nThey need to be held accountable. They've done horrible things.
column6: 很高兴我们想法一致。大多数听我说完都会生气。\n最重要的是，我已经洗心革面了。而我们的敌人没有。\n他们必须承担责任。他们做过骇人听闻的事。

column5: And what's worse — is that they don't see them as wrong.\nThat's why it falls upon our hands to take them down. \nWith that blade? We finally have the means to do it.
column6: 更糟的是——他们并不认为那些事是错的。\n所以我们才必须亲手扳倒他们。 \n有了那把剑？我们终于有了做到的手段。

column5: He's a good man. I've watched him grow into a capable soldier.\nHe always has this way of being happy, no matter the odds.\nEven if we lost almost every rebel, he'd find a way to keep us going.
column6: 他是个好人。我看着他成长为一个能干的战士。\n无论处境如何，他总有办法保持快乐。\n就算我们几乎折损了所有反抗者，他也能找到办法让我们继续前进。

column5: Cracking a joke or two is always in his nature, even in grim circumstances.\nIt can lighten the mood, that's for sure. Nothing is worse than low morale.\nThat's probably what he's best at. Keeping the soldiers happy, and motivated.
column6: 即便在最严峻的时候，讲一两个笑话也总是他的天性。\n那确实能缓和气氛。没什么比士气低落更糟了。\n那大概是他最擅长的。让士兵们开心、有干劲。

column5: I feel the same way. I'm confident that he'll lead us to victory.
column6: 我也有同感。我确信他会带领我们走向胜利。

column5: Yeah, but it works. The morale of our troops is proof of that.\nCold and calculated, but also personable and witty. He's really unique.
column6: 是啊，但确实有效。我们部队的士气就是证明。\n冷酷而精于算计，却又平易近人、风趣机智。他真的很特别。

column5: Tell that to him yourself. I'm sure he'll get a kick out of it.\nHe can lead any way he wants, as long as the army is happy and strong.\nIf you're worried about him getting cocky because of that blade? Don't.
column6: 你自己去跟他说吧。我相信他会很受用。\n只要军队快乐而强大，他想怎么领导都行。\n你担心他会因为那把剑变得自负？不用。

column5: He's aware that The Blade of Exodus isn't a \"free victory\" card.\nThe way he approaches strategy is really something else.\nYou'll probably warm up to him. I know I did.
column6: 他清楚流亡之刃不是一张“免费的胜利”牌。\n他研究战略的方式确实非同一般。\n你大概会渐渐喜欢上他。反正我是。

column5: Absolutely. Everybody lost something special that day.\nFamilies were torn apart, many people lost the will to live.\nA lot of the children only wanted one thing — revenge.
column6: 当然。那天每个人都失去了珍贵的东西。\n家庭被拆散，许多人失去了活下去的意志。\n很多孩子只想要一件事——复仇。

column5: And a lot of the adults {i}saw{/i} one thing — an army ripe for training.\nThey banded together, and The Rebellion slowly became what it is today.\nWe're finally strong enough to {i}do{/i} something; and that's special.
column6: 而许多成年人{i}看到{/i}的是一件事——一支等着被训练成型的军队。\n他们聚到一起，反抗军慢慢变成了今天的样子。\n我们终于强大到可以{i}有所作为{/i}了；这很了不起。

column5: Really? That's news to me. What a bad day to be in Mazeo.\nI guess it makes sense, though. You look like you carry purpose.\nYou'll fit right in. I'm sure almost every rebel could relate.
column6: 真的？这我倒不知道。那真是倒霉的日子，偏偏在马泽奥。\n不过我想这也说得通。你看起来像是身负使命的人。\n你会很融入的。我相信几乎每个反抗者都能感同身受。

column5: Yeah. The bulk of the victims were children who lost their parents.\nFast-forward some twenty-odd years, and they're grown men and women.\nNobody would send children to war. It was important to wait — and train.
column6: 是啊。大部分受害者是失去父母的孩子。\n快进二十来年，他们已是成年的男女。\n没人会把孩子送上战场。重要的是等待——以及训练。

column5: What else were we supposed to do? It's not like we forced them.\nThey wanted to fight — to be trained — and we wanted an army.\nWe were able to achieve unity, and grow into the force we've become.
column6: 我们还能怎么做？又不是我们强迫他们的。\n他们想战斗——想接受训练——而我们需要一支军队。\n我们得以团结一致，成长为如今这支部队。

column5: Yeah. Think about it for a moment. Without them, we'd stand no chance.\nSome people think their future was stolen, but if we win, we can get it back.\nNo occupations, no families being torn apart. That's the true purpose of it all.
column6: 是啊。你想想看。没有他们，我们毫无胜算。\n有些人觉得他们的未来被偷走了，但如果我们胜利，就能夺回来。\n没有占领，没有家庭被拆散。这才是这一切真正的目的。

column5: You don't have to. It's easy to get caught up in the present.\nWhen we win a beautiful future for everybody? That's when you'll see.\nThis is necessary. Their future isn't truly gone — we can take it back.
column6: 你不必明白。人很容易陷在当下。\n等我们为所有人赢得美好的未来时？那时你就会明白。\n这是必要的。他们的未来并非真的消失——我们能够夺回来。

column5: Not really. But it's not numbers that we need. Just strategy.\nThe Triumvirate's Honor Guard is weak. One man could easily kill fifty.\nAnd with that blade on our side, they can't make any more. Just a matter of time.
column6: 不太够。但我们需要不是数量，而是策略。\n三人执政团的荣誉卫队很弱。一个人就能轻松杀掉五十个。\n再加上那把剑站在我们这边，他们造不出更多了。只是时间问题。

column5: That's for sure. Without that blade, we'd never win.\nAs I've always said — we can't take them down with conventional means.\nThere's a lot resting on your shoulders. I hope you're up to the task.
column6: 那是当然。没有那把剑，我们绝不可能赢。\n我早就说过——我们没法用常规手段扳倒他们。\n有很多东西压在你肩上。希望你担得起。

column5: Of course it can. If you don't believe that — you must be new to conflict.\nBattles are fought and won on the war table, far before any sword is drawn.
column6: 当然能。如果你不信——那你一定没经历过冲突。\n战役早在拔剑之前，就已经在作战桌上打完了。

column5: That's not really true. If it were a losing battle, we'd have lost already.\nWe've come this far, and got that blade, precisely because it's {i}not{/i} a losing battle.\nScratch that thought from your mind. You'll come to see that victory is clear.
column6: 那倒未必。如果这是一场必败之战，我们早就输了。\n我们走到今天，拿到那把剑，正是因为它{i}不是{/i}必败之战。\n打消那个念头吧。你会看到胜利是明确的。

column5: Once you master that blade, you'll tear through their very soul.\nMaybe bind them to a suit of armor. I've always been a sucker for irony.
column6: 等你掌握了那把剑，你会撕裂他们的灵魂。\n也许把他们束缚在一副盔甲里。我一直都偏爱这种讽刺。

column5: There's not much to say. He doubled as The Elder of Valinorth.\nYou probably already know everything there is to know. You worked with him.\nThe secrets he kept from you? Well, you've already been told.
column6: 没什么好说的。他同时还兼任瓦利诺斯的长老。\n该知道的事你大概都已经知道了。你曾和他共事。\n他瞒着你的那些秘密？嗯，你都已经被告知了。

column5: He sacrificed himself to get {i}you{/i} that blade. Now he's gone.\nDamek buried him underground, in Mazeo's tunnels. Our new home.\nIn fact, you could see his grave if you wanted. Pay some respects.
column6: 他牺牲了自己，才让{i}你{/i}拿到那把剑。现在他走了。\n达梅克把他葬在地下，马泽奥的隧道里。我们的新家。\n其实，你想的话可以去看看他的墓。去表达些敬意。

column5: I doubt we will. He gave us a hand of winning cards.\nDamek is securing our HQ, and planning our final attack right now.\nWe'll sail to Balteus, and take them down for good.
column6: 我怀疑我们不会。他给了我们一手必胜的牌。\n达梅克正在确保我们总部安全，此刻还在筹划最后一场进攻。\n我们将乘船前往巴尔泰乌斯，把他们彻底扳倒。

column5: I heard that he was. He had a lot of stuff to deal with.\nFinding out about his Father's true role, {i}and{/i} leading Valinorth.\nI can't even begin to imagine what the inside of his head is like.
column6: 我听说他是。他有很多事要应付。\n得知他父亲的真实身份，{i}还要{/i}领导瓦利诺斯。\n我都无法想象他脑子里是什么样子。

column5: I guess it is. But I doubt Damek was thinking that far ahead.\nIt was just the most convenient place to bury his body.\nThose tunnels were being dug up — lots of tools lying around.
column6: 我想是吧。但我不觉得达梅克想得那么远。\n那只是埋葬他遗体最方便的地方。\n那些隧道正在被挖掘——到处都扔着工具。

column5: Lots of pirates, and people who are after money, no matter what.\nDon't trust random people, and don't buy anything from a stranger.\nYou'd get swindled and robbed far before you found anyone genuine.
column6: 有很多海盗，还有很多为钱什么都干得出来的人。\n别随便相信人，也别从陌生人手里买东西。\n你还没遇到一个正经人，就先被坑被抢了。

column5: The occupation didn't make things too much better. It's still dangerous.\nMazeo's spirit idol was also on its final days. Dim and defeated.\nAt least, that's what we thought — until very recently.
column6: 占领也没让情况好多少。那里依然危险。\n马泽奥的精灵灵像也到了最后的日子。黯淡而衰败。\n至少我们一直是这么以为的——直到最近。

column5: Well, there's a church in Mazeo. It's supposed to be for Triumvirate worship.\nAt the altar there, rests a very dim spirit idol. We assumed it was dying.\nBut it's not even the true spirit idol. The true one rests deep underground.
column6: 嗯，马泽奥有座教堂。本该是用来供奉三人执政团的。\n那里的祭坛上摆着一尊极为黯淡的精灵灵像。我们以为它快消亡了。\n但它根本不是真正的精灵灵像。真正的那尊深埋在地下。

column5: The one in the church was merely {i}receiving{/i} energy from the true idol.\nThat's why it was so dim. The source of power was far away.\nNobody knows about this except for The Rebellion. It's our secret.
column6: 教堂里的那尊只是在从真正的灵像{i}接收{/i}能量。\n所以才那么黯淡。力量的源头远在天边。\n除了反抗军，没人知道这件事。这是我们的秘密。

column5: We want to try tapping into it for power.\nIt's our only chance, too — since Alarinthia's idol was destroyed.\nAnd from what I've heard, Valinorth's died out a while back as well.
column6: 我们想试着从中汲取力量。\n这也是我们唯一的机会——因为阿拉林西亚的灵像已被摧毁。\n而且据我所知，瓦利诺斯的那尊不久前也消亡了。

column5: Is that so...? I suppose that's why you're so important.\nIts energy went into you — and now you can wield the blade.\nI hope you don't misuse this gift. I'll admit, I'm a bit intimidated.
column6: 是吗……？我猜这就是你这么重要的原因。\n它的能量进入了你体内——现在你能驾驭那把剑了。\n希望你不要滥用这份恩赐。我承认，我有点忌惮。

column5: I'm not sure. It's one of Alarinthia's many legends.\nApparently, at the dawn of history, The Triumvirate destroyed it.\nThat's why Alarinthia grew into what it is today — an arid wasteland.
column6: 我不确定。那是阿拉林西亚众多传说之一。\n据说在历史的黎明时期，三人执政团摧毁了它。\n这就是为什么阿拉林西亚变成了今天的样子——一片干旱的荒原。

column5: If The Triumvirate did it, we have to wonder why.\nDo the spirit idols pose some threat to their rule...?\nThat's why Damek wants to try tapping into Mazeo's true idol.
column6: 如果是三人执政团干的，我们就得想想为什么。\n精灵灵像是否对他们的统治构成了某种威胁……？\n这就是达梅克想尝试汲取马泽奥那尊真灵像力量的原因。

column5: The Triumvirate suspected it. That's why they were digging in Mazeo.\nBut after twenty years, they found nothing. It was Damek who discovered it.\nWe decided to keep it secret. He's coming up with a plan for it right now.
column6: 三人执政团怀疑过。所以他们才在马泽奥挖掘。\n但二十年后，他们什么也没找到。是达梅克发现了它。\n我们决定保密。他此刻正在为它制定计划。

column5: I suppose so — if The Triumvirate didn't destroy all the others.\nBut right now, the idol in Mazeo is the only one we know about.\nThat is, unless there's one in Balteus. But I doubt it.
column6: 我想是的——要是三人执政团没有把其他的都毁掉的话。\n但目前，马泽奥的灵像是我们唯一知道的一尊。\n除非巴尔泰乌斯也有一尊。但我不觉得。

column5: I mean, The Triumvirate {i}could{/i} have one hidden there. Maybe.\nBut there's no way to know for sure. We should focus on what we {i}do{/i} know.
column6: 我是说，三人执政团{i}可能{/i}在那儿藏了一尊。也许吧。\n但没法确定。我们该专注于我们{i}确实{/i}知道的事。

column5: Yeah. The occupation didn't do much to help, no matter what anyone says.\nI think I'm qualified to speak on the matter. I mean, I've lived there forever.\nThere's still an active piracy network. Smuggling things from Mazeo to Alarinthia.
column6: 是啊。不管别人怎么说，占领都没帮上什么忙。\n我觉得我有资格谈这件事。毕竟我在那儿住了那么久。\n那里还有活跃的海盗网络。从马泽奥往阿拉林西亚走私东西。

column5: Yeah. The elimination of piracy was just an excuse.\nI think they were searching for the spirit idol underneath Mazeo.\nBut what they wanted it for — and what they'd do with it — I have no idea.
column6: 是啊。剿灭海盗只是个借口。\n我觉得他们在寻找马泽奥地下的精灵灵像。\n但他们要它做什么——会拿它干什么——我毫无头绪。

column5: Probably not. Not unless they had some reason to help us. A big one.\nA liberated Alestia would have no room for rampant piracy, right?\nThere'd be no reason to help a cause that hurts their livelihood.
column6: 大概不会。除非他们有某种理由帮我们。而且是很重大的理由。\n一个获得解放的阿莱斯蒂亚不会容忍海盗横行，对吧？\n没理由去帮一个损害他们生计的事业。

column5: Right now, they're a wild card. Not on our side — but not against us, either.\nWe should use that to our advantage while we can. They might turn on us later.
column6: 眼下，他们是张未知牌。不站在我们这边——但也不与我们为敌。\n我们该趁还能利用时加以利用。他们以后可能会转过来对付我们。

column5: I'll be by your side. Damek should be, as well. You'll be fine.\nWe know the lay of the land, and how to deal with people. Just follow our lead.\nBesides, most of our time will be in the Rebel HQ — it's safe there.
column6: 我会在你身边。达梅克应该也会。你不会有事。\n我们熟悉那里的地形，也知道怎么和人打交道。跟着我们走就行。\n何况，我们大部分时间都会待在反抗军总部——那里很安全。

column5: Alestia will be free. We won't have any restriction on trade.\nThat's a good thing, and a bad thing. The pirate will fight against it.\nWe could take down The Triumvirate, only to find ourselves against a pirate army.
column6: 阿莱斯蒂亚将获得自由。贸易不会再有任何限制。\n这既是好事，也是坏事。海盗会反对它。\n我们可能扳倒了三人执政团，却发现自己要面对一支海盗大军。

column5: No. You couldn't even pay me to go back to Alarinthia.\nIt's so hot, it's almost unbearable. And the way they govern things is different.\nI know I say that Mazeo is dangerous, but Alarinthia makes it look like paradise.
column6: 不。你就算付钱我也不会回阿拉林西亚。\n那里热得几乎让人受不了。而且他们治理的方式也不一样。\n我知道我总说马泽奥很危险，但阿拉林西亚让那里看起来像天堂。

column5: I just don't agree with the way things are done over there.\nThe strongest tribe gets to rule the land. It's a constant power struggle.\nEither way, Alarinthia isn't my home. My {i}true{/i} home is Mazeo.
column6: 我只是不认同那边的行事方式。\n最强的部落统治这片土地。永远都在争权夺势。\n不管怎样，阿拉林西亚不是我的家。我{i}真正{/i}的家是马泽奥。

column5: Yeah, and that's especially true in Alarinthia. You choose your home and family.\nYou can change your circumstances if you don't like them.\nOn the mainland, and in Mazeo, it's different. People stay in toxic relationships.
column6: 是啊，在阿拉林西亚尤其如此。你可以选择你的家和家人。\n如果不喜欢自己的处境，你可以改变它。\n在大陆，在马泽奥，就不一样了。人们会困在有害的关系里。

column5: I think of it different. If you don't like your family — find a new one.\nI've spilled enough blood to hold no blind allegiance to it.
column6: 我看法不同。如果你不喜欢你的家人——那就找个新的。\n我流的血已经够多，不会再去盲目效忠什么。

column5: That's a very grim way of looking at things.\nWhen the flames go out, and the ash blows away - you can go back.\nIt still exists. It'll just be a {i}new{/i} Valinorth. Don't be pessimistic.
column6: 你这看法太悲观了。\n等火焰熄灭，灰烬吹散——你就能回去。\n它依然存在。只是会变成一个{i}新的{/i}瓦利诺斯。别这么消极。

column5: He recently rose through the ranks, and has given us tons of trouble.\nWhen The Triumvirate gets in our way — he's likely responsible.\nHe makes himself a lot more \"known\". Way different than the last Inquisitor.
column6: 他最近一路升迁，给我们添了不少麻烦。\n每当三人执政团挡我们的路——多半都是他搞的。\n他让自己“出名”得多。和上一任审判官很不一样。

column5: I haven't gotten to meet his apprentice yet.\nA Grand Inquisitor always has to train one.\nIt ensures a constant cycle of obedience.
column6: 我还没见过他的学徒。\n大审判官总得培养一个。\n这能确保服从的循环延续不断。

column5: I don't know.
column6: 我不知道。

column5: Yeah, but as I said; I have no idea who it is.\nIf Sovy is training him though — I'd watch out.\nSeems like we'll be up against some tough opposition.
column6: 是啊，但我说过了；我完全不知道那是谁。\n不过如果是索维在训练他——那就得小心了。\n看来我们要面对一些难缠的对手。

column5: Not that I'm aware of, and I highly doubt it.\nIt's just them, the inquisition, and their Honor Guard.\nSeems simple enough. But taking them down will be anything but.
column6: 据我所知没有，而且我非常怀疑。\n就只有他们、审判庭，还有他们的荣誉卫队。\n听起来够简单。但要扳倒他们，绝非易事。

column5: The more you know about the enemy, the easier it is to oppose them.\nThis is one of the fundamental rules of war. {i}Know{/i} what you're up against.\nIgnorance on the battlefield is the fastest way to meet your own end.
column6: 你对敌人了解得越多，对抗他们就越容易。\n这是战争的基本法则之一。{i}了解{/i}你的对手。\n战场上的无知是最快送命的方式。

column5: The grass seems to be in immaculate condition.{w}\nWhoever tends to this place must be very passionate.{w}\nIt's more clean than a tavern in the woods has any right to be.
column6: 草坪看起来维护得无可挑剔。{w}\n打理这地方的人一定非常用心。{w}\n它干净得不像林中酒馆该有的样子。

column5: I can smell burning firewood. It must be warm inside.{w}\nThe temperature doesn't really require a fire, though.{w}\nPerhaps it's just for show. To make it more homey.
column6: 我能闻到柴火燃烧的气味。里面一定很暖和。{w}\n不过这个气温其实用不着生火。{w}\n也许只是为了做样子。让它更有家的感觉。

column5: The muffled sound of revelry comes from within.{w}\nIt's pretty lively, given the location of Peregrino.{w}\nI almost can't believe it. It must have a reputation.
column6: 里面传来隐隐约约的欢宴声。{w}\n考虑到佩雷格里诺的位置，这里算是相当热闹。{w}\n我几乎不敢相信。它一定名声在外。

column5: Wow Ulric, it's so big!
column6: 哇，乌尔里克，好大啊！

column5: Yeah, I get compliments on it all the time.
column6: 是啊，我一直因为它的尺寸被人夸。

column5: C-can I touch it...?
column6: 我——我能摸摸它吗……？

column5: Of course you can.\nJust be gentle, though.
column6: 当然可以。\n不过轻一点。

column5: Yeah, I'll do my best.
column6: 好，我会尽量的。

column5: Whoa — it's heavier than I thought!
column6: 哇——比我想的重多了！

column5: You might want to use both hands.\nAnd tighten your grip a little bit.
column6: 你最好用两只手。\n再把握法收紧一点。

column5: Like this...?
column6: 这样……？

column5: A little bit lower.
column6: 再低一点。

column5: Oh, sure.\nHow about now?
column6: 哦，好。\n现在呢？

column5: There you go. That's more like it.\nNow swing that sword with all your might!
column6: 这就对了。这才像样。\n现在用全力挥那把剑！

column5: Hyaa—!
column6: 哈啊——！

column5: Whoa — watch what you're doing!\nYou could've killed me, kid.
column6: 哇——小心你在干什么！\n你差点把我杀了，小鬼。

column5: I'm so sorry! \nI've never used a greatsword before.
column6: 非常抱歉！ \n我以前从没用过巨剑。

column5: I feel like we should keep it that way.
column6: 我觉得你以后还是别用了。

column5: When we enter Peregrino, we're greeted to an argument.{w}\nNormally I'd look around the tavern, but this seemed pretty heated.{w}\nThe barkeep, angry, seems to yell at an annoyed man in front of him.
column6: 我们走进佩雷格里诺时，迎面而来的是一场争吵。{w}\n平时我会四下看看酒馆，但这场争吵似乎相当激烈。{w}\n愤怒的酒保似乎在冲面前一个恼火的男人大喊。

column5: Absolutely not! There's no way!\nTake that letter back to Damek in pieces!\nI'm not giving up my beloved Peregrino, Pro.
column6: 绝对不行！想都别想！\n把那封信撕成碎片还给达梅克！\n我不会放弃我心爱的佩雷格里诺，普洛。

column5: It would seem that he's talking to Pro. The man we came here to meet.{w}\nFor some reason, I find him extremely familiar. I can't pinpoint why.
column6: 看来他是在跟普洛说话。就是我们来这儿要见的人。{w}\n不知为何，我觉得他异常眼熟。却说不清为什么。

column5: Airen, you {i}don't{/i} want to test me.\nThis is for the good of Alestia. Don't be selfish.\nHe wouldn't act outside of our best interests.
column6: 艾琳，你{i}最好别{/i}试探我。\n这是为了阿莱斯蒂亚的利益。别自私。\n他不会做出违背我们最大利益的事。

column5: If you don't agree, he'll cut your funding.\nYou wouldn't be able to keep up, you'd go out of business!\nThis isn't exactly the best place for a watering hole, you know.
column6: 如果你不答应，他会切断你的资金。\n你就维持不下去，会倒闭的！\n你知道，这地方可不怎么适合开酒馆。

column5: The barkeep must be named Airen.{w}\nHe seems to be on the receiving end of Pro's threats.
column6: 酒保一定就是艾琳。{w}\n他似乎正承受着普洛的威胁。

column5: I'll make do! I have to.\nThis place is my home...
column6: 我会想办法的！我必须想办法。\n这地方是我的家……

column5: We're not asking you to move.\nYou just have to let Damek do what he wants.
column6: 我们不是要你搬走。\n你只要让达梅克做他想做的事就行。

column5: I decide to sit back and watch the events unfold.{w}\nAs heated as it seemed, I doubt it would escalate to violence.{w}\nAnd since I'm standing back — even if it did — I'd remain safe.
column6: 我决定退到一旁，看着事态发展。{w}\n尽管看起来火爆，但我怀疑不会升级成暴力。{w}\n而且既然我退在后面——就算真打起来——我也能安然无恙。

column5: You mean turn this place into a barracks!?\nIt's been serving The Rebellion just fine as it is.\nA neutral meeting ground - that's what you all wanted!
column6: 你是说把这地方变成兵营！？\n它一直以现在的样子为反抗军服务得很好。\n一个中立的会面场所——这才是你们当初想要的！

column5: Well now we want something different.\nValinorth needs a line of defense in the future.\nAn army placed here could keep the entire village safe.
column6: 现在我们要的是别的东西。\n瓦利诺斯将来需要一道防线。\n把一支军队驻扎在这儿，就能保护整个村子。

column5: You know Valinorth will be resettled in the future.\nDo you want them to sit there, ready for slaughtering?\nLook me in the eye and tell me your tavern is worth those lives!
column6: 你知道瓦利诺斯将来会重新迁回。\n你想让他们坐在那儿，任人宰割吗？\n看着我的眼睛，告诉我你的酒馆值得用那些人的命来换！

column5: I — I don't know.\nThere must be a way to make this work.
column6: 我——我不知道。\n总该有个两全其美的办法。

column5: We don't have the time to spare!\nWe're about to go to war, if you didn't know.\nDecisions like this {i}need{/i} to be made.
column6: 我们没时间浪费了！\n你不知道的话我告诉你，我们马上就要开战了。\n这样的决定{i}必须{/i}做出来。

column5: But—!
column6: 可是——！

column5: I decide to intrude on their argument before it gets any worse.{w}\nWhat were they arguing about, exactly? That's what I choose to ask first.{w}\nAiren scoffs, and Pro gives me a sly smile, like my interruption benefits him.
column6: 我决定在他们吵得更凶之前插进去。{w}\n他们到底在吵什么？我选择先问这个。{w}\n艾琳嗤了一声，普洛则对我露出狡黠的微笑，仿佛我的插话正合他意。

column5: Damek wants me to shut down Peregrino!\nHe wants to turn it into some stupid barracks.
column6: 达梅克要我关掉佩雷格里诺！\n他想把它变成什么愚蠢的兵营。

column5: It's for Valinorth's safety, you know!\nWith an army here, the village would be safe...\nFuture attacks could be stopped before they even start!
column6: 这是为了瓦利诺斯的安全，你知道的！\n有一支军队在这儿，村子就能安全……\n未来的袭击可以在开始之前就被阻止！

column5: At the cost of my home, you mean!\nI refuse to do this — you can't make me!
column6: 你是指拿我的家当代价！\n我拒绝这么做——你逼不了我！

column5: You're acting like a child, Airen!\nLike I said, you can still live here.\nIt just wouldn't be a tavern anymore.
column6: 你表现得像个孩子，艾琳！\n我说过了，你还可以住在这儿。\n只是它不再是酒馆了而已。

column5: But that's what it was meant to be, Pro.\nThat's what The Rebellion wanted. Neutral ground for both nations.\nYou can't change your mind just because you want something else!
column6: 可它本该就是那样的，普洛。\n那才是反抗军想要的。给两国中立的地盘。\n你不能因为想要别的东西就改变主意！

column5: That's exactly why we {i}can{/i} change our minds!\nAiren, stop being stubborn. Lives are at stake, here!\nLook me in the eyes and tell me your tavern is worth those lives!
column6: 这正是我们{i}可以{/i}改变主意的原因！\n艾琳，别固执了。这里可是人命关天！\n看着我的眼睛，告诉我你的酒馆值得用那些人的命来换！

column5: But—!
column6: 可是——！

column5: Pro cuts him off before he can continue, and looks me in the eye.
column6: 没等他说下去，普洛就打断了他，然后直视着我的眼睛。

column5: Hey, [firstname], give us your input.\nWithout an Elder, {i}you're{/i} in charge of Airen.\nThis place still falls under Valinorth's jurisdiction.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]，说说你的意见。\n没有长老，{i}你{/i}就是管艾琳的人。\n这地方仍属瓦利诺斯管辖。

column5: Hey, [firstname], give us your input.\nWithout an Elder, {i}you're{/i} in charge of Airen.\nThis place still falls under Valinorth's jurisdiction.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]，说说你的意见。\n没有长老，{i}你{/i}就是管艾琳的人。\n这地方仍属瓦利诺斯管辖。

column5: Or do you not know the secret of Peregrino?
column6: 还是说你不知道佩雷格里诺的秘密？

column5: The secret of Peregrino? What does he mean?{w}\nI look at Valessa and Fortaime, and they shrug.{w}\nHe must've recognized me from the blade on my back.
column6: 佩雷格里诺的秘密？他是什么意思？{w}\n我看向瓦莱莎和福泰姆，他们耸了耸肩。{w}\n他一定是从我背上的剑认出了我。

column5: Back when your Elder formed a treaty with Mazeo?\nWell, it's not like they trusted each other immediately.\nBoth sides were scared of walking into a trap.
column6: 当年你们的长老和马泽奥缔结条约的时候？\n嗯，他们也不是一上来就互相信任。\n双方都怕自己走进陷阱。

column5: So what was the best thing to do? Meet each other halfway.\nThat's right. This place was built for secret Rebellion meetings.\nBut things are changing. Valinorth {i}deserves{/i} an army to protect it.
column6: 那最好的办法是什么？各让一步，折中会面。\n没错。这地方就是为了反抗军的秘密会议而建的。\n但情况在变。瓦利诺斯{i}理应{/i}有一支军队来保护它。

column5: It seems like The Rebellion wants Valinorth to be resettled as well.{w}\nThat puts me at ease. I was worried they might throw it away like nothing.{w}\nAll the patrons look pretty happy here, but Valinorth {i}could{/i} benefit from an army.
column6: 看来反抗军也希望瓦利诺斯重新迁回。{w}\n这让我安心了些。我原本担心他们会把它轻易抛弃。{w}\n这里的顾客看起来都挺开心，但瓦利诺斯{i}确实{/i}能从一支军队中受益。

column5: I think about the \"secret\" he just told me. It sort of makes sense.{w}\nA tavern in the middle of the forest isn't the best place to run a business.{w}\nDamek must be lining Airen's pockets to serve The Rebellion's needs.
column6: 我琢磨着他刚告诉我的那个“秘密”。这倒说得通。{w}\n开在森林正中的酒馆可不是做生意的理想地点。{w}\n达梅克一定在往艾琳口袋里塞钱，好让这里满足反抗军的需求。

column5: Don't tell me you're considering this, [firstname].
column6: 别告诉我你在考虑这件事，[firstname]。

column5: Don't tell me you're considering this, [firstname].
column6: 别告诉我你在考虑这件事，[firstname]。

column5: Talk about putting me on the spot. I hope this isn't a frequent event.{w}\nI don't feel like this is my choice, but due to current circumstances — it is.{w}\nMylus resigned as The Elder, leaving me in charge until I elect a replacement.
column6: 真是把我架到火上烤。希望这不是常有的事。{w}\n我不觉得这是该由我做的选择，但眼下的情况——确实如此。{w}\n迈勒斯辞去了长老之位，在我选出继任者之前，由我掌管。

column5: That reminds me. I'd still have to choose between Valessa and Fortaime.{w}\nHowever, it's probably best to take things one step at a time. First — Peregrino.{w}\nI strike a pose that implies I'm in deep thought, but truly, I'm at a loss for words.
column6: 这倒提醒了我。我还得在瓦莱莎和福泰姆之间做选择。{w}\n不过，最好还是一步一步来。首先——佩雷格里诺。{w}\n我摆出一副深思熟虑的样子，但其实，我是不知道该说什么。

column5: Think about it logically for a second.\nIf this was a barracks, Valinorth would be safe.\nWe'd fight off The Triumvirate forces {i}for{/i} you.
column6: 从逻辑上想一想。\n如果这里是兵营，瓦利诺斯就会安全。\n我们会{i}替{/i}你们击退三人执政团的军队。

column5: It may be too late now, but we can plan for the future.\nDamek is {i}requesting{/i} this of Airen, but you can {i}order{/i} it.\nHe'll be expecting answers as soon as we arrive in Mazeo.
column6: 现在或许已经太迟，但我们可以为将来打算。\n达梅克是在向艾琳{i}请求{/i}，但你{i}可以下令{/i}。\n我们一到马泽奥，他就会等着要个答复。

column5: Pro seems to know a lot more than I initially thought.
column6: 普洛知道的比我最初以为的多得多。

column5: He has a point, [firstname].\nTechnically, you're in charge of the entire nation.\nAnd if it sounds like I'm putting pressure on you — I am.
column6: 他说得有道理，[firstname]。\n严格来说，你掌管着整个国家。\n如果听起来像是在给你施压——确实是在。

column5: He has a point, [firstname].\nTechnically, you're in charge of the entire nation.\nAnd if it sounds like I'm putting pressure on you — I am.
column6: 他说得有道理，[firstname]。\n严格来说，你掌管着整个国家。\n如果听起来像是在给你施压——确实是在。

column5: We have a lot to do. We can't waste time over stupid fights.\nHelp them resolve this, so we can talk about {i}important{/i} stuff.
column6: 我们有很多事要做。不能把时间浪费在无聊的争吵上。\n帮他们解决这事，这样我们才能谈{i}重要的{/i}事。

column5: This is all happening so quickly, I can't even find the time to think.{w}\nIt feels surreal, almost like I'm in a dream, or a vision. But it's real.{w}\nAny attempt at collecting my thoughts goes on to be promptly interrupted.
column6: 这一切发生得太快，我连思考的时间都没有。{w}\n感觉很不真实，几乎像置身梦中，或是幻象里。但它是真的。{w}\n每次我试图整理思绪，都会立刻被打断。

column5: There's no reason to turn this into a barracks, though!\nIf you win this war, Alestia will be safe and peaceful.\nDamek is being hasty — he's not thinking straight.
column6: 可是没理由把它变成兵营啊！\n如果你们赢了这场战争，阿莱斯蒂亚就会安全和平。\n达梅克太仓促了——他头脑不清醒。

column5: [firstname], I beg of you. \nDon't take my home away from me.
column6: [firstname]，我求你了。 \n别把我的家夺走。

column5: [firstname], I beg of you. \nDon't take my home away from me.
column6: [firstname]，我求你了。 \n别把我的家夺走。

column5: Everyone stares at me, expecting me to make a decision.{w}\nTheir watchful gaze fills me with anxiety, and I tense up.{w}\nMaybe I should ask for advice before making a decision.
column6: 所有人都盯着我，等着我做决定。{w}\n他们注视的目光让我焦虑，身体也绷紧了。{w}\n也许在决定之前，我该先征求些建议。

column5: Look, I already told you to hurry up.\nThere's no downside to placing an army here.\nAiren is just being whiny, and resistant to change.
column6: 听着，我已经跟你说过快点。\n在这里驻扎军队没有任何坏处。\n艾琳只是在无理取闹，抗拒改变。

column5: You have the chance to prove yourself as a capable leader.\nDon't cave under his demands and give him what he wants.\nAn effective leader does what's best for {i}everybody{/i}.
column6: 你有机会证明自己是个能干的领袖。\n别在他的要求下屈服，别给他想要的。\n一个称职的领袖做的是对{i}所有人{/i}最好的事。

column5: Think about Alestia when you make a choice, not Airen.\nThat advice will help you every time you need to make a decision.\nCatering to individual people is a great way to garner hate.
column6: 做选择时要想着阿莱斯蒂亚，而不是艾琳。\n这条建议在你每次需要做决定时都会有用。\n一味迎合个别人，是招来怨恨的好办法。

column5: Whoa, you actually want my input on this?\nI guess it {i}is{/i} my duty to assist you, but I'm surprised.\nI'm only supposed to guide you when it comes to visions.
column6: 哇，你真的想听我的意见？\n我想{i}确实{/i}有责任协助你，但我很意外。\n我本该只在幻象的事上指引你。

column5: If I had to choose, I'd keep this place the way it is.\nAfter the war, Valinorth, and the rest of the world, will be safe.\nWhy would we train an army {i}after{/i} we've taken down The Triumvirate?
column6: 如果非让我选，我会让这地方保持原样。\n战争结束后，瓦利诺斯，乃至整个世界，都会安全。\n我们何必在扳倒三人执政团{i}之后{/i}还训练一支军队？

column5: If I were The Elder, I'd commit myself to maintaining our independence.\nThat means living outside of conflict, like we've been doing for millennia.\nSiding with The Rebellion, and putting an army here, will tie us to future wars.
column6: 如果我是长老，我会致力于维持我们的独立。\n那意味着置身冲突之外，就像我们几千年来一直做的那样。\n站在反抗军这边，在这里驻扎军队，会把我们卷进未来的战争。

column5: Until today, even {i}you{/i} were raised in an independent Valinorth.\nI can understand a temporary alliance, but we should go back to normal.\nI honestly think it's kind of an insulting idea. We can take care of ourselves.
column6: 直到今天，连{i}你{/i}都是在独立的瓦利诺斯长大的。\n我能理解暂时的结盟，但之后我们该回归常态。\n说真的，我觉得这想法有点侮辱人。我们能照顾好自己。

column5: It's an interesting situation, to say the least.\nBut that doesn't mean the right decision is hard to make.\nWe should ally with The Rebellion, and place an army here.
column6: 这局面至少可以说很有意思。\n但这不代表正确的决定难做。\n我们该与反抗军结盟，并在这里驻扎军队。

column5: If our Elder had done that, then Valinorth would be fine.\nIn my opinion, we need to work toward a united Alestia.\nThat would've saved us this time. It can save us in the future.
column6: 如果我们的长老当初这么做了，瓦利诺斯就会安然无恙。\n在我看来，我们该朝着统一阿莱斯蒂亚的方向努力。\n那样这次就能救我们。将来也能。

column5: Either way, I know you also need to choose a new Elder.\nIf you already have someone in mind, then try to cater to {i}them{/i}.\nIt's important that they're left with a nation they'll be proud to lead.
column6: 不管怎样，我知道你还需要选一位新长老。\n如果你心里已经有人选，那就尽量照顾{i}他{/i}的想法。\n重要的是，留给他们的国家要让他们引以为傲。

column5: I couldn't leave Valinorth defenseless in the future.{w}\nI had to do everything I could to prevent future attacks.{w}\nMy first order as acting Elder was to militarize Peregrino.
column6: 我不能让瓦利诺斯将来毫无防备。{w}\n我必须竭尽所能防止未来的袭击。{w}\n作为代理长老，我的第一道命令就是把佩雷格里诺军事化。

column5: Hmph — I thought you'd be smarter, [firstname].\nStealing people's homes? No better than The Triumvirate.\nI hope you understand what kind of image this gives off.
column6: 哼——我还以为你会更聪明些，[firstname]。\n抢夺别人的家？和三人执政团没什么两样。\n希望你能明白这会给人什么印象。

column5: Hmph — I thought you'd be smarter, [firstname].\nStealing people's homes? No better than The Triumvirate.\nI hope you understand what kind of image this gives off.
column6: 哼——我还以为你会更聪明些，[firstname]。\n抢夺别人的家？和三人执政团没什么两样。\n希望你能明白这会给人什么印象。

column5: I'm not going to argue with you, out of respect.\nValinorth has been my home for ages, and I love the people.\nLook like we're {i}both{/i} losing our homes with no say in the matter.
column6: 出于尊重，我不会跟你争。\n瓦利诺斯长久以来都是我的家，我爱这里的人。\n看来我们{i}俩{/i}都要在这件事上毫无发言权地失去自己的家了。

column5: He crosses his arms and walks off, ensuring I feel guilty.{w}\nWas that really it...? Was my word considered law?{w}\nI don't think I've fully grasped the extent of my power yet.
column6: 他抱起双臂走开了，让我不禁心生愧疚。{w}\n就这样结束了……？我的话被当作法律了吗？{w}\n我觉得自己还没完全领会我权力的分量。

column5: Airen's immediate surrender implies that he was bluffing earlier.{w}\nOr at the very least — he was all talk — trying to intimidate Pro.{w}\nSpeaking of Pro, he turns to me, and gives me a wide smile.
column6: 艾琳立刻屈服，说明他之前只是在虚张声势。{w}\n或者至少——他只是嘴上强硬——想吓唬普洛。{w}\n说到普洛，他转向我，绽开一个大大的笑容。

column5: I couldn't steal Airen's home from him. It was wrong.{w}\nWe'd have to find other ways to keep Valinorth safe.{w}\nForcefully seizing property would give off a bad image.
column6: 我不能把艾琳的家夺走。那是错的。{w}\n我们得另想办法保护瓦利诺斯。{w}\n强行没收财产会给人留下坏印象。

column5: We're above that. We're not like The Triumvirate.
column6: 我们不屑于那种做法。我们不像三人执政团。

column5: Are you serious!? Come on!\nYou can't just leave your village defenseless...
column6: 你是认真的吗！？拜托！\n你不能就这样让你的村子毫无防备……

column5: Now now, Pro. You're the one that brought him into this.\nWe need to take his word as law — that's how it works.\nThank you so much, [firstname]. This calls for a celebration!
column6: 好了好了，普洛。是你把他牵扯进来的。\n我们得把他的决定当作法律——规矩就是这样。\n太感谢你了，[firstname]。这值得庆祝一下！

column5: Now now, Pro. You're the one that brought her into this.\nWe need to take her word as law — that's how it works.\nThank you so much, [firstname]. This calls for a celebration!
column6: 好了好了，普洛。是你把她牵扯进来的。\n我们得把她的决定当作法律——规矩就是这样。\n太感谢你了，[firstname]。这值得庆祝一下！

column5: Airen runs off and starts to prepare some drinks.{w}\nPro crosses his arms and looks at me with a scowl.
column6: 艾琳跑开去准备酒水了。{w}\n普洛抱起双臂，皱着眉看着我。

column5: Thank you {i}so{/i} much!\nWithout you, that would've gone on forever.\nUlric was right. We have other things to tend to.
column6: 真是{i}太{/i}感谢你了！\n没有你，那事会没完没了。\n乌尔里克说得对。我们还有别的事要处理。

column5: He walks over to a nearby table, high-fiving Ulric along the way.{w}\nThe large man looks at me, and nods, signalling his approval.{w}\nBut after that, he walks toward the table as well. Time for a meeting?
column6: 他走向附近的一张桌子，路上和乌尔里克击了个掌。{w}\n那个大个子看着我，点了点头，表示赞许。{w}\n但之后，他也朝那张桌子走去。是要开会了吗？

column5: Just met and you're already a thorn in my side.\nOh well. I just hope you don't come to regret that choice.\nIf you don't, then expect future generations to {i}hate{/i} you.
column6: 才刚认识，你就已经成了我的眼中钉。\n算了。我只希望你别为那个选择后悔。\n要是不后悔，那就等着后代{i}恨{/i}你吧。

column5: Oh well. I guess I should look on the bright side of things.\nAt least they can have a drink while their village burns down again.
column6: 算了。我想我该往好处看。\n至少他们村子再次烧起来的时候，还能喝上一杯。

column5: His sarcasm was noted, and his joke was far too soon.{w}\nHe shrugs at Ulric as he walks to a nearby table and sits down.{w}\nA few moments later, Ulric follows suit. Was it time for a meeting?
column6: 他的讽刺我记下了，而那玩笑开得太不是时候。{w}\n他冲乌尔里克耸耸肩，走到附近一张桌子旁坐下。{w}\n片刻之后，乌尔里克也跟着坐了过去。是要开会了吗？

column5: I wave to Valessa and Fortaime as I walk over to the table.{w}\nA few moments later, we're all seated together, exchanging glances.{w}\nWe wait for someone to break the silence, unsure of what will happen next.
column6: 我朝瓦莱莎和福泰姆挥了挥手，然后走向那张桌子。{w}\n片刻之后，我们都坐到了一起，互相交换着眼神。{w}\n我们等着有人打破沉默，不知道接下来会发生什么。

column5: Ulric.
column6: 乌尔里克。

column5: Pro.
column6: 普洛。

column5: I thought you might find yourself here.\nDamek must know about the new plans, then?
column6: 我就想你可能会在这儿。\n那达梅克一定知道新计划了？

column5: He assumed you were slacking off.\nNow that I'm here, I guess it's half true.
column6: 他以为你在偷懒。\n既然我来了，我想这算是说对了一半。

column5: Don't worry, I had it planned all along.\nYou can doubt me, but everything worked out.\nHere we are — all together, and ready to plan.
column6: 别担心，我早就计划好了。\n你可以怀疑我，但一切都成了。\n我们在这儿——齐聚一堂，准备好谋划了。

column5: I need to get all of you back to Damek, as fast as possible.\nWe need to make some moves, and plan our final attack.
column6: 我得尽快把你们全都带回达梅克那儿。\n我们需要采取些行动，筹划最后一场进攻。

column5: He looks at me, and then at the blade on my back.
column6: 他看了看我，又看了看我背上的剑。

column5: You'll be training under a pretty strict regiment.\nDamek wants you to master that blade as fast as you can.
column6: 你会接受相当严格的训练。\n达梅克希望你尽快掌握那把剑。

column5: Now, I already told you about the spirit idol they found in Mazeo.\nDamek wants to use you, and that blade, to tap into its power.\nHe thinks it will give us more of a chance to win this war.
column6: 那么，我已经跟你说过他们在马泽奥发现的那尊精灵灵像了。\n达梅克想利用你，还有那把剑，来汲取它的力量。\n他认为这能让我们更有机会打赢这场战争。

column5: If you aren't already aware, a new spirit idol was found in Mazeo.\nDamek thinks we can use you, and that blade, to tap into its power.\nHe thinks it will give us more of a chance to win this war.
column6: 如果你还不知道，马泽奥发现了一尊新的精灵灵像。\n达梅克认为我们可以利用你，还有那把剑，来汲取它的力量。\n他认为这能让我们更有机会打赢这场战争。

column5: Wait, a {i}new{/i} spirit idol!? I didn't know that could happen.\nI thought we had all of them mapped out for a long time.
column6: 等等，一尊{i}新的{/i}精灵灵像！？我不知道还能这样。\n我以为所有的灵像早就都被记录在案了。

column5: I'll assume your studying abilities are limited in Valinorth.\nBut the occupation was just a cover for The Triumvirate's true goal.\nThey were looking for this spirit idol — so they could destroy it.
column6: 我猜你们在瓦利诺斯的学习条件有限。\n但那次占领只是三人执政团真正目的的掩护。\n他们在找这尊精灵灵像——好摧毁它。

column5: Whoa, hold on!\nWhy would they want to do that...?
column6: 哇，等等！\n他们为什么要那么做……？

column5: We don't know. But that's why Damek wants it first.\nThere's a possibility that it poses a threat to their reign.\nLegend has it, they destroyed Alarinthia's idol as well.
column6: 我们不知道。但这就是达梅克想先得到它的原因。\n它有可能对他们的统治构成威胁。\n传说他们还摧毁了阿拉林西亚的灵像。

column5: Wait — Alarinthia's idol was destroyed?
column6: 等等——阿拉林西亚的灵像被摧毁了？

column5: It was so long ago that they almost never had one.\nThat's why it turned into the arid wasteland its become.\nKind of like how Valinorth will freeze over — potentially.
column6: 那是太久以前的事了，他们几乎像从没有过灵像一样。\n这就是它变成了如今这片干旱荒原的原因。\n就像瓦利诺斯可能会冻结冰封一样——有可能。

column5: So Damek wants to use this new spirit idol for power?\nIsn't that risky? Does he even know what will happen?
column6: 所以达梅克想用这尊新的精灵灵像来获取力量？\n那不是很冒险吗？他到底知不知道会发生什么？

column5: Nope, this has never been done before.\nUnless, of course, we're talking about your friend here.
column6: 不知道，这种事从来没人做过。\n当然，除非说的是你这位朋友。

column5: He stares directly at me. He must be talking about my power.{w}\nIt was gifted to me directly from Valinorth's now-dim spirit idol.
column6: 他直直地盯着我。他一定是在说我的力量。{w}\n那是瓦利诺斯如今已黯淡的精灵灵像直接赐予我的。

column5: You mean he wants to use the power on people!?
column6: 你是说他想把那股力量用在人身上！？

column5: As far as I know, yeah.\nIt could give our army {i}just{/i} the push it needs.\nThere's even a chance it could turn them into Seers.
column6: 据我所知，是的。\n它可能会给我们的军队{i}恰好{/i}需要的那股推力。\n甚至有可能把他们变成先知。

column5: An... army of Seers?\nUlric, do you realize how crazy that sounds?\nI can't believe Damek would want to do that!
column6: 一支……先知组成的军队？\n乌尔里克，你意识到那听起来有多疯狂吗？\n我真不敢相信达梅克会想做这种事！
